Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation, I'll be using the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us identify any areas where you might need additional support.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings with me, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for our conversation. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as smooth and comfortable as possible.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a judgment, but rather an opportunity for us to work together to ensure you're receiving the care and support you need during this significant life transition. So, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been a struggle to find the humor in things like I used to. I mean, I still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or seeing the silly faces she makes, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm going through the motions a lot of the time, and even when I do laugh, it doesn't feel as genuine or as often as it used to. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think to myself, "I should be enjoying this more," but the feeling just isn't there. It's like the happiness is muted or something. I don't know, it's hard to explain. I just feel really tired and overwhelmed most of the time, and it's hard to find the energy to laugh or see the funny side of things.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I've been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but not as much as I used to. Like I said, it's just not the same. There are moments when my baby does something adorable, and I'll laugh, but it's fleeting. The sadness and worry seem to creep back in pretty quickly. I feel like I'm just pretending to be happy sometimes, you know? Like, I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think, "Oh, this is supposed to be the happiest time of my life," but the feeling isn't really there. It's like I'm just going through the motions. And then I feel guilty for not feeling happy enough, which just makes things worse. Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll think about upcoming events or activities, but I don't really feel that excitement or anticipation that I used to. Even things that I normally enjoy, like meeting up with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, you know? Taking care of the baby and managing the household is just so overwhelming, and it's hard to think about enjoying things when I'm just trying to keep up. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, and then I'll just feel anxious about how I'm going to manage it with the baby, or if I'll be able to get everything done that I need to. It's like the joy has been sucked out of things, and I just feel really drained and overwhelmed all the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not doing things right. Like, if the baby is crying, I'll think, "Oh, it's because I'm not feeding her right," or "I'm not burping her right." Even when my partner tries to reassure me that everything is okay, I still can't shake the feeling that it's my fault somehow. And it's not just with the baby - it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I'll think, "I'm a terrible mother and a terrible wife because I'm not keeping the house clean enough." It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself, and it's really hard to stop those thoughts. Sometimes I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I'm doing wrong, and it's hard to focus on anything else. It's like I'm my own worst critic, and it's really exhausting.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

.. yeah. That's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if someone breaks into the house? It's just this constant stream of worst-case scenarios running through my head, and it's really hard to shut it off. Sometimes I'll be awake in the middle of the night, and I'll just be lying there, worrying about all these things that might happen. And it's not just about the baby, either - it's about everything. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and the house and everything else. It's just this feeling of constant unease, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. And the worst part is, I know it's irrational - I mean, the baby is healthy, and we're safe, and everything is okay... but my brain just won't stop worrying. It's really exhausting, and it's hard to enjoy anything when I'm always on edge like that.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and that's when the panic sets in. Other times, it's just out of nowhere - I'll be doing something normal, like folding laundry or making dinner, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. It's like my body is reacting to something, but my brain doesn't know what it is. It's really hard to describe, but it's like my whole body is on high alert, and I just feel like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. And the worst part is, it's not just the panic itself - it's the fear of losing control, of not being able to take care of the baby or myself. It's a really scary feeling, and it's hard to shake. Sometimes I'll try to calm myself down by taking deep breaths or going for a walk, but it's not always easy to make the feeling go away.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely true. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a full-time job, and on top of that, I'm trying to manage the household and take care of myself, and it's just feeling really overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and the laundry is piling up, and the dishes are piled up in the sink, and I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I'm not doing, like cooking healthy meals or exercising or spending quality time with my partner, and that just adds to the feeling of being overwhelmed. It's like I'm constantly playing catch-up, and I'm just not doing a very good job of it. Sometimes I'll have a good day, and I'll feel like I've got everything under control, but then the next day will come, and it'll be like I'm starting all over again. It's really exhausting, and it's hard to see a way out of it. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of overwhelm, and I don't know how to break free.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been happening to me a lot lately. I'll be lying in bed, and my mind will just start racing with all these worries and thoughts, and I won't be able to fall asleep. Or, I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be wide awake, thinking about all the things that are stressing me out. It's like my brain won't turn off, and I just can't relax. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are really disturbing, and they'll wake me up feeling anxious and on edge. It's like my body is just wired to be "on" all the time, and I don't know how to calm it down. I've tried all sorts of things to help me sleep - warm baths, reading before bed, avoiding caffeine - but nothing seems to be working. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the fact that I'm so unhappy and stressed out all the time. I feel like I'm just walking around in a fog, and I don't know how to clear it. Sometimes I'll go days without getting a good night's sleep, and it just makes everything feel so much harder. I feel like I'm running on empty, and I don't know how to refill my tank.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been a big part of my experience lately. I feel like I'm just sad all the time, and I don't know how to shake it. It's not just that I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed out, it's like there's this deep sadness inside of me that I just can't escape. Sometimes it feels like it's suffocating me, and I don't know how to breathe. I'll be doing things that I normally enjoy, like spending time with my baby or talking to my partner, and I'll just feel this sadness underlying everything. It's like I'm wearing this mask of happiness, but underneath, I'm just feeling really miserable. And it's hard to explain, because I know that I should be happy - I have a beautiful baby, a loving partner, a comfortable home... but none of that seems to be enough to lift this sadness. Sometimes I'll just start crying, and I won't even know why. It's like my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I'm not even aware of what's triggering it. It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get it back. I just feel so... stuck. And the worst part is, I feel like I'm a bad mother, because I'm not feeling the way I'm supposed to feel. I'm supposed to be happy and grateful and in love with my baby, but instead, I just feel sad and overwhelmed and scared.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like I just can't hold it in anymore, and I'll just start sobbing for no reason. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so sad and hopeless. I'll be in the middle of doing something, and I'll just start crying, and I won't even know why. It's like my emotions are just right there on the surface, and it doesn't take much to set me off. I've been trying to hide it from my partner and family, because I don't want to worry them, but it's hard to keep it inside. Sometimes I'll just go into another room and cry, because I don't want anyone to see me like that. It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling so much emotion all the time, and I don't know how to process it all. The crying is just a release, I guess. It's like my body is just trying to let it all out, because I'm not able to deal with it in any other way. It's scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to get it back. But at the same time, it's like my body is trying to tell me something, and I need to listen. I just wish I knew what it was trying to say.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, struggling to hold back tears) Yeah... I've had those thoughts. They're scary, and I don't know where they're coming from. It's like, I know I'm a good person, and I would never hurt anyone, but sometimes... (pauses again, taking a deep breath) sometimes I just feel like I don't know how to keep going. It's like the sadness and the overwhelm are just too much, and I don't know how to escape it. And then these thoughts come into my head, and they're just... they're really disturbing. I don't want to think about them, but they're there. (looks up, tears streaming down her face) I don't want to hurt myself, I really don't. I love my baby, and I love my partner, and I don't want to leave them. But sometimes, in the darkest moments, it feels like... it feels like it might be a way out, you know? (shakes her head) I know it's not a solution, and I know it's not what I want. But the thoughts are there, and they're really scary. (pauses, collecting herself) I'm sorry. I didn't mean to cry. It's just... it's really hard to talk about this stuff. (looks down, wiping away tears)
